<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff (route, a path literal in AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dcb5fb3ef30b373aae040476e84e1df84cec77d2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `98f4b7b27cdb659778e87a8c853df3dfe05937e8` — the merge of head `3e59db0af0da68805e35387a3ee09e806d0cdd2a` into base `dcb5fb3ef30b373aae040476e84e1df84cec77d2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 98f4b7b27cdb659778e87a8c853df3dfe05937e8 && git checkout 98f4b7b27cdb659778e87a8c853df3dfe05937e8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dcb5fb3ef30b373aae040476e84e1df84cec77d2 3e59db0af0da68805e35387a3ee09e806d0cdd2a && git checkout -B drift-repro dcb5fb3ef30b373aae040476e84e1df84cec77d2 && git merge --no-ff 3e59db0af0da68805e35387a3ee09e806d0cdd2a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dcb5fb3ef30b373aae040476e84e1df84cec77d2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dcb5fb3ef30b373aae040476e84e1df84cec77d2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · not yet ACCEPT · head `fe2b8b490760c17fd94327e74624b83b3f60747b`

**维护者：这个 PR 现在还不要合并。** 它要等 #29979 和 #30004 先落地，再补下面三项，然后才做契约复审并交你审。PR 正文里“请审阅并合并”指的是那之后。

Read from the diff on GitHub, not from the report:

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #29997`, no other closing keyword in the body. No `content/docs/releases/` change. `one-time-token-handoff.js` is not exported from the package entry, so its new names reach no public surface, which supports `Clause-②: no`.
- **Route order:** every `400` is still decided ahead of the new answer, the token path is unchanged, and `redirect` is rebuilt from the validated parameters.
- **Surface beyond the claim:** `examples/app-showcase/playwright.config.ts` (one env line) and a doc comment in `showcase-smoke.live.test.ts`, needed for the browser test. Accepted.
- **Browser test is nightly, not per PR:** the card asked for CI, and the reasons in Acceptance notes hold up against the spec. Accepted. A Console upgrade that breaks this shows up the next night, not on its own PR.

**Owed in one patch round, after #29979 lands:**

1. **Page half.** Carry the `handoff_refused_at` branch in `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/handoffRedirect.ts` with tests in this PR. The #29979 seat agreed that if #29979 lands first, this card carries both halves (comment 6620189624; the update is on #29979). This keeps it in the same release, and it is what makes the changeset's "cannot bounce" true.
2. **Spec docblock (published text).** On `OneTimeTokenHandoffQuerySchema`, the `302 to sign in` line says a page navigation gets it, and the `401` line says "a request that is not such a page navigation". A navigation reporting `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` is a page navigation and gets the `401`. State that case.
3. **Module docblock.** "It cannot bounce" and "the second holds even for a page that ignores the first" need the condition this PR's own body gives: a browser with no Fetch Metadata can still bounce until the page half is present.

Then re-run the browser spec at the merged tree. The page half also moves this PR's file surface; the claim is updated at that point.

**Maintainer brief correction:** 风险与回滚 says 旧版 App 不受影响. No released app uses this flow yet (the card says so), so there is no older app to affect. The seat's final brief will say that.

**Open, for the review or for #30010's next round:** `resolveHandoffSignInEntry` calls `server.fetch` with `env` but no execution context. On a host whose middleware reads one, that could throw, end in `onUnserved`, and leave the JSON `401`. Read from the diff, not measured. objectstack-ai/cloud#3549 is where it would first matter.

**Out-of-scope findings:**
- Cloud offers no route or scheme: already filed as objectstack-ai/cloud#3549.
- `principal-session-console-boot.dogfood.test.ts` skipping in CI: stays in Acceptance notes. It is not a product defect, and no maintainer order covers it, so it is outside the filing gate.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `584f1e43fc38715b02a0bec34de48a5f4228c39c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/one-time-token-handoff.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/handoffRedirect.ts (at this head, reviewed under the maintainer's widening 「并入复审」), ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/LoginPage.tsx and ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/RegisterPage.tsx as merged on main at f35b361997 by #29979 (reviewed under the widening); cited and read, not reviewed: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (getConsolePageUrl, getAuthIssuer, getCanonicalOrigin), packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts (readShellConfig, the 503 responder), ui/apps/console/src/utils/consoleBase.ts, scripts/check-auth-mount-ledger.mjs. The rest of the diff (the changeset, examples/app-showcase/e2e/mobile-signin-handoff.spec.ts, playwright.config.ts, showcase-smoke.live.test.ts, the three test files) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `GET /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff` gains one answer: `302` to this deployment's sign-in page for a page navigation whose session is missing or older than five minutes, on a process that serves that page. Every other answer is unchanged, and every refusal keeps its place: cross-site `400` first (line 498), then the closed query set, the scheme, the challenge and the method (506–544), all before any session is read (`validated` is built at 548, `sessionCreatedAt` at 552); `401` for a non-navigation, for a `same-origin` navigation and for an unserved page. Right. The app's anonymous probe (`Accept: application/json`, no `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`) still reads `401`: `isPageNavigation` is false for it, pinned.
2. The token-bearing `302` (578–580) is untouched: same `withHandoffChallenge` binding, same `Location` of `redirect_uri` plus `token`, same `NO_STORE`. Right.
3. `packages/spec`: docblock only. `OneTimeTokenHandoffQuerySchema`, `AuthEndpointPaths.oneTimeTokenHandoff` and every export are unchanged; `Spec property liveness` and both `Check Changeset` runs green; the dev reports `check:generated` clean. No accept-set moves. Right.
4. `plugin-auth` package surface: `one-time-token-handoff.ts` is not among `src/index.ts`'s `export * from` lines, so the new exports (`HANDOFF_REFUSED_AT_PARAM`, `HandoffSignInEntry`, `isPageNavigation`, `resolveHandoffSignInEntry`) and the new REQUIRED `HandoffDeps.signInEntry` are package-internal; the only constructor of `HandoffDeps` outside tests is `auth-plugin.ts`, which supplies it. Right.
5. `auth-plugin.ts`: no new mount. The existing `rawApp.get(basePath + '/one-time-token/handoff')` gains `signInEntry`; the in-process probe is a `rawApp.fetch(...)` call inside the handler, not a mount verb, so `check:auth-mount-ledger` has nothing new to read. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` green. Right.
6. Ledger note: text only and consistent with point 1 (five-minute mint, root-relative `302` to the sign-in page, the three `401` cases). Right.
7. Console: `handoffRedirect.ts` adds `HANDOFF_REFUSED_AT_PARAM`, `handoffRefusedAt` and an optional `refusedAt` on `isHandoffSessionFresh`; `useHandoffRedirect`'s signature is unchanged, so `LoginPage` and `RegisterPage` on main pick the mark up through the hook with no edit. Additive. Right.
8. Check-runs on this head: 25 success, 10 skipped, 0 failure, 30 in_progress. Not yet read (running at review time, not awaited): Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Lint UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · debt ledger, Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16. Those are the CI families that run the route's and the page's unit tests; their conclusions stand on their own and this record does not pre-empt them.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29997-handoff-signin-entry.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/console` at `patch`; `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the changeset body and on the PR body. Matches the diff: no spec schema, export or generated artefact moves, so `Clause-②: no` is right; no metadata key, value or default changes hands, so `none` ⇒ `patch` under AGENTS.md Post-Task 3 (the level follows the kind, not the `feat(` prefix). The three packages named are the three the diff moves, and all sit in the `fixed` group, so they version together. `Check Changeset` green. PASS.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []`; the flags are the report's `deviations` and the PR's NOT MEASURED lines.

- **Real `ASWebAuthenticationSession` / Custom Tabs headers not measured.** Answered as far as code goes: when neither `Sec-Fetch-Dest` nor an HTML `Accept` arrives, both arms fall to the `401` JSON that is today's answer, so a surprise there costs the new redirect, never a wrong one. Reviewer's reading, also unmeasured here: Chrome (Custom Tabs) has sent Fetch Metadata since 76 and WebKit (ASWebAuthenticationSession) since iOS 16.4; every browser names `text/html` in `Accept` on a top-level navigation, which is the fallback. Escalated to the maintainer as the one assumption objectstack-ai/mobile#190 measures first.
- **The mark is a server time, not the bare mark the #29979 thread agreed.** Judged right: `SocialSignInButtons` defaults `callbackURL` to `window.location.href`, so a provider's fresh session returns under the mark, and a bare mark would hold the form over it — the Google users this flow exists for. A time lets a later `createdAt` forward. Flagged for the maintainer's ratification because it changes an agreed arrangement; no code objection.
- **The browser test is nightly, not per-PR.** The card asked for it "in CI"; it runs in Nightly Tiers from `examples/app-showcase/e2e` because `Live E2E UI` serves the Console from `vite preview` with no backend mount for the redirect to land on. Escalated: a Console change that breaks this flow shows the next night, not on its own PR. A real deviation from the acceptance note with a stated cause; the maintainer decides whether a per-PR lane is worth building.
- **The `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` carve-out.** Answered in ④: it is the second stop of the loop, and it costs a stale URL reopened from history a JSON stop instead of a form. Stated in the spec docblock. Fine.
- **No execution context on the probe.** Answered: `c.executionCtx` is read nowhere in this repo or in objectstack-ai/cloud (grepped both); `@hono/node-server` hands `env` alone; the probe passes the outer `c.env` (`{incoming, outgoing}`), and the one reader of it in this repo (`readTransportPeerAddress`, guarded, `incoming.socket.remoteAddress`) resolves to the same client; no writer of `env.outgoing` exists in the repo. Precedent: `readShellConfig` dispatches the same way on every Console document. The pin for an unguarded reader (keep the `401`, log `it answers 500`) is present.
- **Landing order.** #29979 merged at f35b361997 and #30004 at d9895a17fa, both on main; the showcase `webServer` env line resolves against `OS_TRUSTED_APP_SCHEMES` on main. Nothing is left to land first.
- **"Noted, not filed".** The `registerUrl` mark drop in `LoginPage.tsx` on main is judged in ④ and needs its own card. The dogfood skip and cloud#3549 are outside this scope.
- **Verification ran UNLOCKED on macOS.** A declared narrowing of the dev's local runs, not of the code; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts here.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts` (hits) — against the maintainer's order on #29997 and the route as its first consumer.** Every sentence of the new docblock was read against `runOneTimeTokenHandoff` at this head. "Every `400` decided before any session is read" holds (the session is read at 552, after the last `400`). The `302`-to-sign-in conditions (a page navigation, no fresh session, a deployment that serves the Console, not `same-origin`) are exactly `refusedSessionAnswer`'s three gates. "Root-relative so the browser stays on this origin" holds: `Location` is a pathname plus a query. The `401` list is complete. Two imprecisions, should-fix: (a) the docblock says the sign-in `Location` carries `redirect` and omits `handoff_refused_at`, which the route also writes — defensible because the page's route is declared out of contract, but the published list of what `Location` carries should not be shorter than what it carries; (b) "a deployment that serves no Console" is wider than the code's test, which is "this PROCESS answers the sign-in page with 200 text/html" — a Console served by a front proxy also keeps the `401`, which the route module docblock says and the spec docblock does not. Neither misleads an app: the app never parses this `Location`.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/one-time-token-handoff.ts` (widened).** Tried to break it:

- *Send a token elsewhere.* The sign-in `302` carries no token; the token `302` is untouched. Nothing attacker-controlled reaches `Location` unencoded: `redirect` is built from `validated` (the three parameters, after every refusal) through `URLSearchParams`, so a CRLF, a second `?` or a `redirect_uri` with any character cannot escape its value; `signInPage` and `handoff` are config paths. Holds.
- *Send the browser off-origin.* `Location` takes `new URL(getConsoleUrl('/login')).pathname` — a path, never the canonical origin; pinned (`canonical.example.com` never reaches `Location`, `uiBasePath: '/console/'` honoured). One config-only gap, should-fix: `getCanonicalOrigin` strips ONE trailing slash, so a `baseUrl` ending in `//` composes `https://h//_console/login`, whose pathname is `//_console/login`; `deploymentBase` then resolves to `/`, `localPath` to `/_console/login`, the probe is served, and `Location: //_console/login?…` is protocol-relative — the browser leaves for a host named `_console`. Not reachable from a request (config alone), every mailed link of that deployment is already broken the same way, and no token rides that redirect; still, the page refuses a `redirect` that starts with `//` and the route should refuse a `signInPage` or `handoff` that does, as unserved.
- *Forge `handoff_refused_at` or `redirect` to skip the five-minute rule.* The page's verdict decides forward-or-form and nothing else; the route re-reads the session's `createdAt` on its own clock on every request, and a forwarded old session gets `401`. A forged mark mints nothing. Holds.
- *Hold a person out.* A link crafted with a far-future mark holds that page's form even after a sign-in on it (no `createdAt` is later than it) — but only on a URL the attacker built; the app's own entry gets the route's `now`. Equivalent to any broken link; no gain. A mark of `0` makes the page forward an old session into the `401` JSON — the #29979 behaviour on main today. Holds.
- *A malicious app or page.* Everything the new `302` lets a navigation reach was reachable by opening `/_console/login?redirect=…` directly (card, Security). The cross-site `400` is still first and still judged only when the header is present (ruling A); an old browser without Fetch Metadata keeps exactly the exposure ruling A accepted, no more. An `iframe` or a `fetch` asking for HTML gets `401` (`Sec-Fetch-Dest` outranks `Accept`, pinned). No new capability. Holds.
- *Loop.* Two independent stops, both pinned: the page holds any session not created after the mark (it reads no request header, so it holds with or without Fetch Metadata), and the route answers `401` to a `same-origin` navigation it refuses, which is the only way the page forwards. The residual — a stale URL reopened after five minutes with a session created after the mark, or a session the page reads and the route cannot — ends at `401` JSON with Fetch Metadata, or at one more redirect whose newer mark holds the form without it. Neither repeats. The dev's 228-requests-in-20-s reading at the pre-guard head is the control. Holds.
- *A host where the Console or the headers differ.* `--no-ui`, an unbuilt Console's `503`, a Console that redirects elsewhere, a `200` that is not HTML, a `uiBasePath` that composes no URL: each pinned to `401` with one `warn`. A base path in `baseUrl` is kept in what the browser is told and stripped from what this process is asked, pinned both ways. The probe carries no cookie and `Accept: text/html` only, and it cannot re-enter this route (its path is the Console's; Hono matches the mount exactly). Cost: one in-process document fetch per refused navigation, plus the Console's own `readShellConfig` hop — bounded, no recursion; an observation, not a finding.
- *Clock.* The docblock's "two readings of one clock" is true per process; on a multi-node deployment behind one host it is one clock per node, and a refusal stamped on a node ahead of the node that then signs the person in holds the form for the skew's duration (each sign-in makes a later `createdAt`, so it clears). Should-fix as a docblock caveat; NTP skew is far under the time a sign-in takes.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts` (widened).** Wiring only: `getConsoleUrl('/login')` is the composer every mailed sign-in link already uses (`auth-manager.ts:2793`), `getAuthIssuer()` the base the published `iss` carries, `basePath` the mount. `reportedNoHandoffSignInPage` is a per-mount once-flag. No new mount, nothing for the ledger gate. Holds.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts` (widened).** The note matches ① point 1. Holds.

**`ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/handoffRedirect.ts` (widened, at this head).** `handoffRefusedAt` accepts digits only and refuses a non-safe integer (`'9'.repeat(400)` → `null` → the age check decides, pinned). `isHandoffSessionFresh` with a mark compares two server timestamps and never reads `now`; without one it is unchanged. `useHandoffRedirect` reads the mark in the same layout effect that reads the clock, once per session identity, so a sign-in on the form re-judges with the new session. `handoffNavigationTarget` (merged by #29979, unchanged here) refuses `//`, off-origin and lookalike paths and re-serialises what it checked. Holds.

**`LoginPage.tsx` / `RegisterPage.tsx` as merged on main (widened).** The hand-off branch runs before the organization steps and only by `window.location.assign(handoff.target)` (same-origin, as the route requires), guarded by `mobileHandoffStartedRef`; a held session shows the form (`signInNeeded = !user || handoff.holdForSignIn`). The SSO branch (`client_id` plus `redirect_uri` at the top of the query) is checked first, which is why the route keeps the app's `redirect_uri` nested inside `redirect` (pinned). The non-hand-off path keeps `isSafeRedirect` plus `withConsoleBase`, so the hand-off exception is not a general way out of the mount. Holds, bar one finding. **Should-fix, already merged (#29979), needs its own card:** `LoginPage.tsx:328` builds `registerUrl` as `/register?redirect=…` and drops `handoff_refused_at`, and `RegisterPage.tsx:171` bounces a closed sign-up to `/login?redirect=…` the same way; a person holding an old session on a device whose clock is behind who follows Sign up is judged by the age check alone and forwarded into the route's `401` JSON (the same-origin stop). It stops and never loops, and this PR does not depend on it, so it does not count against this verdict. The fix is one line in each page: carry the mark.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: the spec docblock's two imprecisions; a `//` guard on `signInPage` and `handoff`; the multi-node clock caveat; the `registerUrl` and `/login`-bounce mark drop (merged code, own card).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-29997-handoff-signin-entry`
Reviewed-by: `session_c967d7a472b0485c94711bfcb22159c8`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts` (hits) — against the maintainer's order on #29997 and the route as its first consumer.** Every sentence re-read against `runOneTimeTokenHandoff` and `resolveHandoffSignInEntry` at this head: "every `400` decided before any session is read" holds; the `302`-to-sign-in conditions are exactly `refusedSessionAnswer`'s three gates plus the entry's served test, now stated as the code tests it; `Location` root-relative with `redirect` and `handoff_refused_at` holds; the `401` list is complete, including the fronted-Console case. The docblock says what the code does, no more and no less. Holds.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/one-time-token-handoff.ts` (widened) — the delta, tried to break it:**

- *The `//` guard.* It reads the parsed `pathname` of two config URLs after `URL` normalisation, so the shapes that could slip a second host past a string test are already flattened: a backslash in a special-scheme path becomes `/` before the test; `%2F%2F` stays percent-encoded and is a same-origin path, not protocol-relative; a `?` or `#` never reaches `pathname`. Only a leading `//` names another host in a `Location`, and only that is refused. The guard sits after `deploymentBase`/`localPath` are computed and before the probe, so a refused path costs no in-process fetch (pinned: `fetch` not called) and the `warn` names the offending path and both config keys. `handoff` is now built once and the same value is tested and returned. Nothing request-controlled reaches either input. Holds.
- *Everything else* (token elsewhere, off-origin `Location`, forged mark or `redirect`, holding a person out, a malicious app or page, the loop, a host where the Console or the headers differ) is as judged on 584f1e43fc: unchanged code, same pins, holds.

**`ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/handoffRedirect.ts` (widened) — `handoffMarkQuery`, tried to break it:**

- *Can the mark reach a link that is not a hand-off redirect?* No: the first gate is `handoffNavigationTarget(redirect) === null ⇒ ''`, the same exact-path, same-origin, no-`//` match the forward itself uses, so a lookalike path (`HANDOFF_PATH + 'X'`), another route (`/settings`, `/api/v1/data/x`), an absolute URL, an empty or null redirect all yield the empty suffix — pinned, and pinned again on the real pages (CONTROL: beside `/settings` the links are what they were, mark or no mark).
- *Can it inject anything into those URLs?* No: the suffix is built from `handoffRefusedAt(search)`, which returns a safe integer or `null` after a `^\d+$` test, so the only text that can follow `&handoff_refused_at=` is digits; `redirect` beside it is `encodeURIComponent`-ed as before. A mark of `soon`, `1e3`, `-1`, `9` × 400 or a percent-encoded value yields no suffix (pinned). The `&` is correct in all three callers because each suffix is only ever appended after a `?redirect=` segment that is present whenever the suffix is non-empty.
- *Does anything change for a page with no hand-off?* No: with no `redirect` the links are the bare `/register` and `/login`; with a non-hand-off `redirect` they are byte-identical to main; with a hand-off `redirect` and no mark on the page they are byte-identical to main — all three pinned. `handoffMarkQuery` reads `window.location.search` at call time, which is the page's own query in both the render-time builders and the closed-sign-up effect; its default guards `typeof window === 'undefined'`.
- *Does the carried mark change the receiving page's verdict correctly?* Yes: `RegisterPage` reads it through the same hook, and its new pins show the form held for a session not created after the mark, a sign-up on the form forwarding, and a session created after the mark forwarding on a device whose clock is ahead. Holds.

**`LoginPage.tsx` / `RegisterPage.tsx` at this head (widened).** The hand-off step itself (before the organization steps, by `window.location.assign`, guarded by the started-ref, form held for `holdForSignIn`) is unchanged from main and holds as judged before. The three link changes are the delta above. `registerUrl` is also handed to `InvitationSignUpPrompt`, and `loginUrl` to the register form's Sign in link; both carry the suffix only beside a hand-off redirect, which an invitation redirect never is. Holds.

**The road the mark does not reach: `/verify-email-prompt`.** Three hops drop it: `LoginPage`'s `onError` for `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` builds a fresh `URLSearchParams` of `email` and `redirect` (LoginPage.tsx:568–571), `RegisterPage`'s `onVerificationRequired` does the same (RegisterPage.tsx:349–352), and `VerifyEmailPromptPage.handleBackToLogin` rebuilds `/login?redirect=` alone (main, :101–104). Consequence, read from the code: a person who arrived with a mark, tried an unverified account (the server refuses before any session is made, so the browser's session is whatever it held on arrival), and pressed Back to login is judged by the device-clock age check alone; with an old session that the device's clock reads as young, the page forwards into the route's `same-origin` `401` JSON. It stops and cannot loop (the route never redirects a `same-origin` navigation; without Fetch Metadata it redirects once with a newer mark and the form holds). It needs four conditions at once (an old session in the system browser, which iOS's ephemeral session never has; a device clock behind by about the session's age less five minutes; an unverified account; the Back to login button), and its worst outcome is the pre-#29997 JSON answer.
